The list can be short: the Future resolves as soon as one value is available and does not wait for a full batch. Terminal states stay values: the Future resolves with the `CLOSED` / `PEER_GONE` sentinel. An ``n`` past the drain quantum (2048) resolves with at most one quantum per pass. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ``n`` is less than 1. [ConcurrentUseError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A blocking receive on this side from another thread races the armed async consumer: a side is confined to one thread and one consumer form at a time. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} Single and batch waiters on one channel resolve in call order. A batch waiter takes up to its ``n`` values from the available burst. It takes at least one value when reached, so a batch reached late in a busy pass can resolve short. Cancellation, timeouts, ``spin=True``, and consumer exclusion follow [`recv_async()`](`pymizu.Channel.recv_async`). A declined foreign payload ahead of a batch resolves it short with the preceding values. The waiter that reaches the declined message rejects with [`ForeignPayloadError`](`pymizu.ForeignPayloadError`). Later waiters are unaffected. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#aeddc19e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pymizu with pymizu.Channel.create(''' import pymizu while True: x = ch.recv() if x is pymizu.CLOSED: break ch.send(x) ''') as ch: ch.send_batch([1, 2, 3]) batch = await ch.recv_batch_async() batch ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: :::
